title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Police Officer Entrance Exam
summary: Explore First Contact, Accounts and Evidence, Principles and Precision, Calm Under Pressure, Professional Judgment across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Listen closely. Think clearly.
Follow the facts.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: First Contact, Accounts and Evidence, Principles and Precision, Calm Under Pressure, Professional Judgment. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official police recruitment, legal, fitness, medical, psychological or employment assessment. Laws and operational procedures vary by jurisdiction.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

police-q1.question: You arrive at a scene where someone faces an immediate threat. What is the first priority?

answers.a1: Protect life and make the scene as safe as possible
answers.a4: Work out who is legally responsible

police-q2.question: Which opening question is most likely to produce a witness’s own uninterrupted account?

answers.a1: The person in red started it, correct?
answers.a2: Please tell me what happened from the beginning
answers.a3: You did not see the whole incident, did you?
answers.a4: Was the suspect angry or frightened?

police-round1-new1.question: What should an initial scene update distinguish?

answers.a1: Observed facts from unverified reports

police-round1-new2.question: Why give an exact location when requesting help?

answers.a1: It helps responders find the right place
Paying attention and checking understanding

police-round1-new4.question: Which statement is an observation rather than an assumption?

answers.a1: The window was broken when I arrived
answers.a2: The occupant must have broken it
answers.a3: The suspect was obviously angry earlier

police-q3.question: Why may witnesses be kept apart before their initial accounts are taken?

answers.a1: To make the interviews shorter
answers.a2: To decide who is most confident
answers.a3: To reduce the chance that their memories influence one another
answers.a4: To guarantee that every account matches

police-q4.question: What is the main purpose of a documented chain of custody?

answers.a1: To rank evidence by importance
answers.a2: To prove a suspect owned every item
answers.a3: To replace photographs of the scene
answers.a4: To record who handled evidence and preserve its integrity

police-round2-new1.question: Why record a witness's own words accurately?

answers.a1: To preserve their account without adding assumptions
answers.a2: To guarantee their memory is perfect

police-round2-new2.question: What should happen if an officer does not understand an important instruction?

answers.a1: Seek clarification

police-round2-new3.question: What is the purpose of an evidence label?

answers.a1: Linking an item to its documented identity and handling record

police-round2-new4.question: Which detail belongs in a factual incident note?

answers.a1: The time and action actually observed

police-q5.question: Which set of principles best describes responsible use of police powers?

answers.a1: Lawful, necessary, proportionate and accountable

police-q6.question: In the international spelling alphabet, which word represents the letter B?

answers.a1: Baker
Assessing people and evidence without improper bias
answers.a4: Ignoring evidence that challenges a theory

police-round3-new2.question: Why declare a relevant personal connection to a case?

answers.a1: So a potential conflict can be managed
answers.a4: To make the connection confidential from supervisors

police-round3-new3.question: Which word represents C in the international spelling alphabet?

answers.a1: Charlie

police-round3-new4.question: Which word represents D in the international spelling alphabet?

answers.a1: Delta

police-q7.question: Which approach is most consistent with de-escalating a tense but non-immediate situation?

answers.a1: Speak rapidly and move closer without warning
answers.a2: Issue several competing instructions at once
answers.a3: Use calm, clear language, listen and allow safe space
answers.a4: Raise your voice before anyone else can speak

police-q8.question: When safe and practical, what should happen before an important item at a scene is moved?

answers.a1: It should be cleaned
answers.a2: It should be shown to every witness
answers.a3: It should be placed with similar items
answers.a4: Its original position and condition should be documented

police-round4-new1.question: Someone is upset but presents no immediate threat. Which response supports de-escalation?

answers.a1: Explain calmly and allow them time to respond

police-round4-new2.question: A language barrier prevents understanding. What is a sensible step?

answers.a1: Arrange suitable interpretation under the applicable process
answers.a3: Raise your voice instead of clarifying

police-round4-new3.question: Why reassess safety as an incident develops?

answers.a1: Conditions and risks may change
answers.a2: The first assessment is never useful
answers.a3: Every incident becomes less risky with time

police-round4-new4.question: What should a concise handover include?

answers.a1: Key facts, current risks and outstanding actions
answers.a3: Only the ending of the story

police-q9.question: You discover a factual error in a report you submitted. What is the most professional response?

answers.a1: Report and correct it promptly through the proper process
answers.a2: Wait to see whether anyone notices
answers.a3: Delete the entire report without a record
answers.a4: Ask a colleague to take responsibility

police-q10.question: Which radio message is most useful during a fast-moving incident?

answers.a1: A long personal theory with no location
answers.a2: A concise factual update with the exact location and help required
answers.a3: Several unconfirmed rumours delivered at once
answers.a4: A vague request to send someone somewhere

police-round5-new1.question: What should happen to newly found evidence that challenges an initial theory?

answers.a1: It should be recorded and assessed fairly
answers.a3: It should be hidden until the case ends
answers.a4: It should be changed to fit the theory

police-round5-new2.question: Why separate certainty from uncertainty in a report?

answers.a1: So readers can assess what is established and what needs checking
answers.a2: To make the report sound less professional

answers.a1: Being able to explain and justify actions through proper review

police-round5-new4.question: Which principle remains important when procedures differ between countries?

answers.a1: Follow applicable law and authorised procedures
answers.a2: Use a foreign rule without checking
answers.a3: Assume all powers are identical worldwide
answers.a4: Treat a quiz result as official authority
